title: Pre/postcondition annotations
description: The core annotation: requires (what must hold on entry) and ensures (what holds on exit). A binary search annotated with 'requires sorted(a)' and 'ensures result is the index or -1' states its contract completely; verifiers (Dafny, Frama-C) prove the code meets it.
method: Annotate functions with requires/ensures; the verifier generates proof obligations; the SMT solver discharges them.
usage: Annotate module boundaries first; make postconditions strong enough to be useful to callers.

demo.code:
print('requires: sorted(a)')
print('ensures: (result == -1) or (a[result] == key)')
print('verifier: PROVED for all inputs')

title: Frame conditions (modifies clauses)
description: Postconditions say what changed; frame conditions say what didn't. 'modifies balance' declares the function touches only the balance — everything else is unchanged. Without frames, verifiers must assume the worst; with them, modular reasoning works.
method: Declare modifies sets; the verifier checks only listed state changes; callers rely on everything else being preserved.
usage: Write modifies clauses on every mutating function; keep them minimal and honest.

demo.code:
print('modifies: balance')
print('caller knows: name, history untouched -> modular proof composes')

title: Specification inheritance
description: Subclasses must honor their parents' contracts: preconditions can only weaken, postconditions only strengthen (behavioral subtyping, Liskov). Spec inheritance is checked mechanically — an override that strengthens a precondition is rejected, protecting every caller relying on the parent contract.
method: Check override preconditions (weaker or equal) and postconditions (stronger or equal); reject violations at compile/verify time.
usage: Verify overrides against parent contracts; document intentional strengthenings.

demo.code:
print('override requires x > 0 (parent: x >= 0) -> STRENGTHENED precondition')
print('verifier: REJECTED (breaks substitutability)')

title: Assertion checking at runtime
description: Annotations don't have to be proved statically — Eiffel, CodeContracts, and Ada compile them to runtime checks. Runtime assertion checking catches contract violations in testing with precise blame, and serves as the fallback where static proof is infeasible.
method: Compile annotations to checks; run the test suite; violations name the broken contract; use as a bridge to full verification.
usage: Enable runtime checks in test; use violations to find missing preconditions before attempting proof.

demo.code:
print('runtime: requires sorted(a) violated by test_t7')
print('blame: caller test_t7 -> precondition missing, fixed')

title: Annotation inference
description: Writing annotations by hand is the bottleneck; inference (Daikon for invariants, Houdini for candidate annotations) proposes them automatically, and the verifier keeps the true ones. Human effort shifts from writing specs to reviewing inferred ones — annotation at scale.
method: Infer candidate annotations from runs or syntax; filter by verification; present survivors for human review.
usage: Infer first, then strengthen by hand where the property matters most.

demo.code:
print('inferred 34 candidate invariants; verifier kept 21')
print('human review: 21 accepted, 3 strengthened')

title: Gradual verification
description: Full verification is expensive; gradual verification lets teams verify the critical 5% statically and check the rest at runtime, with a soundness story for the mixture. Like gradual typing for proofs — adopt verification incrementally without boiling the ocean.
method: Verify critical modules statically; runtime-check the rest; the framework guarantees the combination is sound.
usage: Verify the money paths statically; runtime-check the rest; expand the verified core over time.

demo.code:
print('payments/: statically verified; ui/: runtime-checked')
print('gradual guarantee: verified core sound, rest monitored')

title: Model-based specifications
description: Model-based specs describe behavior via mathematical models — a set is specified as a mathematical set, a map as a function — independent of implementation. Clients reason about the model; the implementation refines it. JML and Eiffel use model queries to give specs implementation-independent meaning.
method: Define model queries (mathematical views); specify operations on models; prove the implementation refines the model.
usage: Specify containers and ADTs via models; clients program to the model, not the representation.

demo.code:
print('model: set<int> contents')
print('add(x) ensures contents = old(contents) + {x} -> proved vs model')

title: Termination measures (decreases)
description: Total correctness needs termination: the decreases clause names a well-founded measure that shrinks each iteration/recursion. Binary search decreases hi-lo; the verifier proves it can't decrease forever, so the loop must end. No measure, no termination proof.
method: Provide a decreases expression; prove it decreases and stays bounded below; the verifier checks both.
usage: Find the measure when designing the loop; exotic loops need lexicographic measures.

demo.code:
print('decreases: hi - lo')
print('each iteration: hi-lo shrinks, >= 0 -> TERMINATES')
